root_cause.text: AppArmor’s DFA differential-encoding verifier in `security/apparmor/match.c` used a single temporary mark for both “currently being checked” and “already verified” states, and it also used the wrong loop-state comparison when bailing out on backward transitions, allowing malformed diff-encode chains with loops to be accepted as valid.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a separate `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED` bit in `match.h`, changes `verify_dfa()` to detect “loop in current chain” via `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE` while using `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED` for already-verified states, and removes the old `if (k < j) break; /* already verified */` logic because it was comparing the wrong iterators and misclassifying backward steps as verified transitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new marker flag to track verified diff-encoded matches.
intent_record.what: A new macro definition, `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED`, was added with the value `0x10000000` between the existing flag definitions and the `MATCH_FLAGS_MASK` constant.
intent_record.how: This extends the set of available bit flags for match encoding state, allowing code elsewhere to mark a diff-encoded entry as verified without reusing existing flag bits.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix DFA verification by adding explicit in-progress versus verified marking to avoid incorrect chain handling and loop detection.
intent_record.what: The loop condition in `verify_dfa()` was changed to stop on `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED` instead of `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE`, an added check now aborts when a chain element is already marked with `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE`, the old `k < j` early-exit was removed, and a second loop was added to clear `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE` and set `MARK_DIFF_ENCODE_VERIFIED` on states after verification.
intent_record.how: This changes DFA verification from using a single transient mark to a two-phase marking scheme: it first detects loops/self-loops and avoids reprocessing chains already being verified, then promotes verified states to a permanent verified marker so later traversals can distinguish completed verification from in-progress marking.

The group directly matches the root cause: it changes AppArmor DFA verification to use explicit in-progress versus verified state marking, addressing the loop-handling and incorrect chain validation flaw in `match.c`.

The root cause describes malformed differential-encoding chains with loops being incorrectly accepted because the verifier’s state-handling/loop-check logic was wrong; this check is within the verifier path that decides whether transition links are valid.
